text:
Maria Alvarez: FYI — noticing big p95 latency spikes for a private VPC customer after last runtime deploy (~09:09 UTC). p50 ~20ms -> p95 ~450ms, throughput dropped ~3x, only on private-usw2 cluster.
SRE-bot: alert: egress-nat-conntrack-high — conntrack ~65700 > threshold 65000. NAT gateway returning TCP_RESETs. See alert stream: https://internal.ops/redwood/egress
Thomas Lee: grabbing profiler dumps now. Observed kernel-selector fallback to 'cpu' kernels for ~20% of inferences (sequence length variance + small batch sizes). Also seeing kv cache hit rate tank.
Thomas Lee: kv stats snapshot:
```
kv_cache_hits: 12450
kv_cache_misses: 7650
hit_rate: 61.9%
pool_backlog: 420 -> 1800
cpu_kernel_pct: 19.6%
conntrack_count: 65712
/proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_local_port_range: 32768 61000
```
Joel Park: sounds like a thundering-herd at the NAT: many short-lived outbound connections -> ephemeral port exhaustion -> conntrack blowup -> TCP resets. That then stalls requests and forces kernel-selector to pick slower CPU paths while the runtime queues. Batching backlog spike suggests runtime opened more concurrent conns instead of reusing connections.
Maria Alvarez: proposed quick mitigations: 1) enable SNAT port reuse + tcp_tw_reuse on the node pool, 2) temporarily increase nf_conntrack_max, 3) if that helps, follow with runtime change to connection pooling and a batch-size floor. Can infra try sysctls on a canary?
Neha Patel: applying sysctl changes to canary (private-usw2-canary): `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=200000` and `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range='20000 65535'`. Also toggling `net.ipv4.tcp_tw_reuse=1`.
infra-oncall: patched firewall NAT timeout from 300 -> 120s for ephemeral flows to reduce conntrack churn; rolling to 2 nodes first.
Thomas Lee: after the sysctls + fw tweak, re-sampled stats:
```
kv_cache_hits: 19840
kv_cache_misses: 1250
hit_rate: 94.1%
cpu_kernel_pct: 3.2%
conntrack_count: 14210
```
Thomas Lee: p95 back down to ~38ms on the canary, throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline. Monitoring for 30m.
Maria Alvarez: great. Follow-ups: runtime PR to add connection pooling + a guard in kernel selection to avoid fallback on transient connection stalls, and a batching heuristic floor so tiny chats don't force extra concurrent conns. I'll open INFRA/RUNTIME tickets and link logs.
Joel Park: also adding an eval harness to replay small-chat traffic patterns so this shows up in perf tests. :thumbsup:
SRE-bot: incident resolved: p95 restored. follow-up ticket created: INFRA-1239
